function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

### What the **`triangulation_metrics`** function does | Item | Description | |------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Pulls a list of *products* and *branches* that have had at least one “triangulation” run in the most recent 90 days (or a custom window you specify). | | **Return format** | A JSON array where each element represents a single product‑branch pair that has been processed. Each element contains:
• `product_id` – the unique ID of the product.
• `branch_id` – the unique ID of the branch.
• `last_run_date` – ISO‑8601 timestamp of the most recent triangulation run for that pair.
• `run_count_90d` – how many times that pair ran in the past 90 days.
• `status` – `"active"` if the branch is still enabled, `"inactive"` otherwise. | | **Typical use‑case** | Quickly identify which product‑branch combinations are actively being triangulated so you can monitor performance, spot gaps, or trigger downstream processes. | --- ### How to call it ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get( url="https://api.example.com/triangulation_metrics", headers={ "Accept": "application/json" }, params={ "days": 90, # optional – defaults to 90 "end_date": None # optional – defaults to today }, cookies={ "session_id": "abc123", "auth_token": "def456" } ) data = response.json() print(data) ``` #### Parameters | Parameter | Type | Default | Notes | |-----------|------|---------|-------| | `days` | int | 90 | Number of days back from `end_date` to consider. | | `end_date` | str (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | `None` (today) | End of the look‑back window. | | `headers` | dict | `{}` | Include `Content-Type`, `Accept`, etc. | | `cookies` | dict | `{}` | `session_id`, `auth_token`. | | `timeout` | float | 5.0 | Seconds to wait for a response. | | `allow_redirects` | bool | True | Follow redirects automatically. | | `verify` | bool | True | Verify SSL certificates. | --- ### Example output ```json [ { "product_id": "P001", "branch_id": "B12", "last_run_date": "2026-06-20T14:32:00Z", "run_count_90d": 7, "status": "active" }, { "product_id": "P002", "branch_id": "B07", "last_run_date": "2026-05-15T09:10:00Z", "run_count_90d": 2, "status": "inactive" } ] ``` Use this data to feed dashboards, alerting systems, or further analytics pipelines.
